A. There are no known cases of a perfectly photographic memory.

The concept of a "photographic memory" is often misused and misunderstood. While some individuals may have exceptional memory abilities, there is no scientific evidence to support the existence of a completely photographic memory (1).

According to the British Psychological Society, people with exceptional memory abilities often have specific strengths, such as exceptional recall of factual information or the ability to recognize patterns (2). However, these abilities are not the same as having a perfectly photographic memory.

The notion of a perfect photographic memory is often associated with claims of individuals having an "eidetic memory," which is a rare and not fully understood phenomenon. Research on eidetic memory suggests that it may be related to exceptional attention, perception, and encoding abilities, but it is not a common trait (3).
